fields.why: The Medicare footnote names 'persons aged <65 years who are receiving disability benefits' as an eligibility pathway; receipt of disability benefits reads as access/entitlement rather than a clinical condition, so B's population entry is defensible, but it describes Medicare generally and the brief's 'framed as social position or access' rule does not clearly reach it. Level 0 either way.

The Discussion offers 'more ready access to medical care' as a possible explanation of the higher Northeast prescribing rate, an explanation of an outcome; the brief records determinants even below level 4, and none of its exclusions (recommendation, unmeasured confounder, service disruption) applies.

brief_issues: The brief does not say whether an eligibility pathway quoted from a program's general description (e.g. Medicare via disability benefits) counts as a population-defining SPD; a rule that only the article's own population definition counts would settle it.
